notes.heading: Old Addison standards, ordinances 084-033 and 085-059
items: The streets' rights of way are widened to 80 ft to allow on-street parking, and the alley to 25 ft for fire lanes. Adjacent property owners pay for the streets, parking, alleys, sidewalks and streetscape.
Buildings must be in a turn-of-the-century, small-town style. The Architectural Review Committee reviews all new construction and changes, and approves exterior materials.
Fire protection: 2-hour fire walls between all buildings, monitored alarms in all buildings, and a fully automatic sprinkler system.
No development may use more than one-third of its floor area for restaurants unless it provides the required restaurant parking.
Deliveries are made at the rear, not from the street, and waste is kept in enclosed areas.
Signs must be approved by the Architectural Review Committee and fit the district's theme.

notes.heading: Lots 8 and 9 (4815 Broadway), ordinance 085-091
items: The final plan is approved, and development must follow it.
A fully automatic fire sprinkler system must be installed before the building is occupied.
Water service must be improved before any building permit, and the site must be platted.
Landscaping escrow is shared by each owner's land area.

notes.heading: Lot 10 (4819 Broadway), ordinances 084-017 and 085-071
items: Development must follow the attached development plans, and the final plan was approved in 1985.
Landscaping goes on the front of the site, and the applicant must follow the recommendations of the Fire Department and Building Inspections.
Water service must be improved before any building permit, except a foundation permit. Landscaping escrow is shared by each owner's land area.

notes.heading: Broadway frontage, ordinances 084-016 and 085-059
items: On-street parking on Broadway counts toward an adjoining property's on-site parking, in proportion to lot area.
085-059 allocates the 52 Broadway spaces across 47,194 sq ft of developable land, which is 1.1 spaces per 1,000 sq ft.
